matches.quote: The 0.7 eV PrNiO2 peak is assigned to Pr 5d hybridized states and then "disregarded" without independent evidence
Five parameters (J1–J4, J⊥) are fitted to a single dispersion per compound ... The authors should report the fit covariance or correlation matrix
no direct evidence of order is shown ... a dispersion consistent with LSW does not establish long-range 3D order.
The PrNiO2 d_z² energy (2.96 ± 0.58 eV, Table I) is essentially unconstrained, so the statement that it is "possibly larger" than in the cuprate should be removed
quantified (for example crossed/total ratios per peak, data versus calculation) ... the d_xy intensity mismatch at H = 0.4 (σ) is attributed to Pr 5d or interstitial s states
A finite energy at Γ could also come from ... an artefact of the elastic/phonon subtraction ... show the Γ-point spectra, their decomposition
Fig. 2(a) shows a sum of spectra over H = 0.4–0.475, across which the magnon disperses, which broadens it.
The magnon damping comparison with Bi2201 does not isolate self-doping ... compare with Sr-doped infinite-layer nickelates ... or a differently reduced reference film
Different substrates and strain states are not addressed in the cross-compound comparison. ... The authors should state the strain state of each film
The suggestion of stripe order from the (0.2,0.2) dispersion maximum and the extra elastic intensity beyond (0.25,0.25) (p. 5) is unsupported
Near Γ the magnon energies are comparable to the phonon ... and the Γ-point error bars in Fig. 3(a) are the largest of the dataset.
its fitted position is sensitive to how these are constrained ... The authors should: state which fit parameters ... were free, fixed or shared across Q
The crystal-field parameters (10Dq/Ds/Dt or orbital energies), spin–orbit coupling, exchange field, core-hole lifetime and broadening behind the calculations in Fig. 4(g–l) are not given.
that the magnon (J⊥) result gives "a proof of fully occurred topotactic reduction … and absence of interstitial oxygen atoms" does not follow
Δ = 8.00 eV was "chosen sufficiently larger than U also providing reasonable results" ... those references give effective one-band U values, not the on-site multiplet Hubbard U

notes: C8 raises the concern that apparent dispersion could come from varying weights of overlapping nondispersive peaks for the magnon; the review raises this exact mechanism in detail for the d_xy orbital peak (P15) and for the low-Q magnon/phonon/elastic overlap near Gamma (P3), so C8 is scored as partly raised via P3. C2 (excess oxygen as dopant) and C3 (extrinsic/impurity origin of the 0.7 eV peak) are scored as partly raised because P21, P22 and P23 question the Pr 5d assignment of the 0.7 eV peak, the proof of absence of interstitial/excess oxygen, and single-phase reduction completeness without explicitly framing excess oxygen as the effective dopant or citing impurity-diffraction correlations.
